title: How Priyam Raj built Moise.ai in college and sold it for ₹1 crore+
summary: Priyam Raj tells how he built Moise.ai, a YouTube video-idea predictor, as a college student in a small city, got early traction by tweeting and tagging YouTubers, scaled to about 4 lakh a month, and sold it on Acquire.com for six figures to avoid platform risk. The lesson is that execution on the right timing beats college pedigree, idea quality or even naming.

principles.text: Build something that solves your own problem, and make it unique rather than another to-do list or mobile app.
principles.quote: I wanted to build something unique and something that solved my issue my personal issues something like that.

principles.text: Ride a fresh tech wave (AI) and pair it with a niche you know, like tools for YouTubers.
principles.quote: because AI hike was out there already, I combined that and came up with the idea of moise.ai.

principles.text: Early on, a name or domain doesn't matter much; use whatever domain you have and ship.
principles.quote: if you think names matter in businesses because I don't think it does so much if you're just starting out.

principles.text: Get early distribution by posting about the product and tagging the creators who would use it.
principles.quote: I started mentioning a lot of YouTubers on Instagram and Twitter both by tagging the usage of the tool

principles.text: Sell a product that depends on a platform before the platform can absorb the feature and wipe out revenue.
principles.quote: this is something that YouTube could have just released in like one day inside the creator dashboard.

principles.text: Execution matters more than ideas or pedigree; where you study or live is irrelevant.
principles.quote: it does not matter where you're studying where you're from if you are the best
